details:
What it does and how it works

Luno: A Little World in Space is an interactive video game that functions as a lunar base simulator. The player takes on the role of an astronaut who must survive the various difficulties of being on a lunar base. The core gameplay loop revolves around resource management: players must attend to critical needs such as radiation protection, food production, and energy supply. The primary mechanic is that every decision made by the astronaut carries a cost in terms of resources, forcing the player to prioritize and think strategically.

Benefits and intended impact

The intended impact of the project is highly educational, specifically targeting students between 7 and 12 years old. It teaches them what the day-to-day life of a real space mission is actually like. Beyond scientific facts, the main benefit is character-building: we teach "the power of focus" by demonstrating that concentration and discipline are vital skills to survive. Ultimately, our goal is to inspire future explorers by bringing players closer to the real pressure of keeping a space mission afloat.

How our project is creative & Team considerations

Our main creative innovation is the concept of "combat-free survival". Our team considered that in real space exploration, there are no aliens to fight; instead, the only enemy is the clock and the failure of the ship's systems. We successfully transformed the repetitive tasks of base maintenance into an adrenaline-filled routine, making it a dynamic and addictive challenge. To ensure this high-tension, technical scenario wasn't overwhelming for children, we deliberately chose a friendly and accessible PixelArt style for our objects, maps, and environments.

Tools, coding languages, and software used

To develop this project, we integrated real space data and used various software tools:

  • NASA Resources: We utilized official NASA images of the Moon to accurately reference and design our lunar environments and backgrounds.
  • Game Engine & Code: We developed the core mechanics using TurboWarp and programmed the logic using Block Programming.
  • Art & Design: All the PixelArt assets, objects, and mapswere created using piskel.
  • Presentation: We used Canva and Youtube to design our pitch and presentation materials.
